ruling.description: A plastic mug made from ABS plastic, which is pink and red in colour. It has inscriptions on it stating "Ava" and "Giggle Monster", with a face containing eyes and a mouth with three teeth (one on top, two on bottom) depicting a "monster" style face. There are two feet at the bottom of the mug, each with three toes coming off it, with black toenails designed in the shape of triangles. The mug can be personalised to replace the name at the top of the mug above the monster to whatever name the customer prefers, using a non-toxic marker over a label, which is removed to complete. The barcode on the bottom of the mug is made of paper with a glossy lamination, specifying that the mug is not suitable for hot drinks or microwaving. The mug measures 102 mm width x 84 mm depth x 105 mm height.

ruling.description: A personalised bracelet made from recycled plastics, 40% polyester, 18% polyurethane (pre-consumer), 37% polyurethane and 5% calcium carbonate. There is a brass metal, plated with chromium connecting the bracelet with a leather band inside to layer the bracelet together. There are ties made of kraft paper and iron securing the bracelet to the kraft box. The box measures 94.5 mm width, 94.5 mm height and 14.5 mm in diameter, with an acrylic glue dot to secure the lid and base together in the centre, with an additional glue dot to to secure the flap of the box in place. The box is personalised to include a specific name, with the words "saving the world ONE bracelet at a time" underneath. There is also a laminated gift tag with a white adhesive sticker. The bracelet comes with a male and a female version. The male version has a clasp measuring 23mm x 8mm, and a weave with a width of 6.5-7mm. The length of the bracelet is 210mm. The female version has a clasp measuring 22mm x 7mm, the weave has a width of 5-5.5mm, and the length of the bracelet is 197mm. The box has a detail of a circle on the top left corner of the front of the box which says, "RECYCLED MATERIALS", similarly it has a circle in the bottom right corner which says, "NEW LIFE TO USED PLASTICS". The box is packaged in a biodegradable bag.

ruling.description:
The uplink power control system is an electronic device designed to maintain stable uplink signal power from earth station radio frequency terminals to geostationary satellites, compensating for signal reduction caused by weather conditions such as rain, ice or snow.

The system constantly monitors beacon signal loss using an internal or external receiver and automatically increases or reduces uplink power as needed. It can either adjust power using one reference signal or using a comparison mode which enables more accuracy. 

The system adjusts transmission power in real time using feedback from the signal receiver, increasing or reducing power in 2 dB increments across a range of 2-20 dB to prevent equipment overload and to maintain optimal link quality.  

The system includes built‑in safety features that allow it to keep working and protect the equipment if a fault or signal loss occurs. It can be monitored and controlled from the front panel or remotely and includes a backup system for reliability. The unit has a compact 1RU rack-mountable design and is securely packaged in protective packaging.

The mechanically perforated pegboard panels are made from SPCC cold-rolled steel sheets.  Also provided with the pegboard are steel metal hooks and tool-holder set for use with spanners, screwdrivers, pillars etc and removable plastic storage bins for small parts such as screw, nuts, bolts etc.  Hooks, tool holders and bins can be inserted into the slots and positioned in a number of different ways depending on usage. The product is flat packed into corrugated cardboard cartons for transport.  The product is sold as a complete kit ready for installation.

A semi-finished round cornered square steel bar with a cross-section throughout its length. 
Sizes ranging from 95mm square up to 250.7mm square 

The main molten steel production methods include:
Melting raw materials using either an Electric Arc Furnace or Basic Oxygen Furnace
Ladle Furnace refining
Vacuum Degassing
Chemical adjustments in the tundish
After this stage, the steel solidifies through two different methods:

Continuous casting into oscillating moulds to produce Blooms, which accounts for most of the material used in Lincoln
Bottom teeming into Ingots, which is employed for a limited tonnage

Once Blooms and Ingots are cast, the solidified steel divides into two types used in our forging process:

As-Cast Blooms (not included in this classification)
Hot rolled Blooms and Ingots feature “smooth” surfaces, which may be mill-finish, lightly scaled, or shotblasted. 

Steels with higher hardenability chemistry may be annealed after rolling to lower the risk of cracking during transit.
During forging, the steel is heated above 1,175°C, fully converting its crystalline structure to Austenite. This process eliminates previous microstructures like Ferrite, Pearlite, Bainite, and Martensite present in the imported steel. These may reform during cooling but are typically refined compared to the original as-rolled or as-cast structures. For precipitation hardening grades, forging at high temperatures also acts as a solution treatment, dissolving precipitates formed during rolling. The size and distribution of these precipitates are further modified by controlled cooling. Forging alters grain size and distribution throughout the steel.

Initially, imported steel has limited useful mechanical properties. The desired properties are established during forging—through solution treatment and precipitation hardening—or via traditional heat treatments post-forging, such as Quenching and Tempering, Normalising, or Isothermal Annealing.

Imported bars arrive in a Round Cornered Square cross-section, but none of these shapes remain in the finished product.

Black powder coated rack rails, typically manufactured from carbon steel, with standardised rack unit (U) hole spacing in accordance with the 19 inch rack format. Holes may be square for cage nuts or pre tapped threaded holes for screw fixing.
They are mounting racking components, designed for permanent installation in standard 19 inch server and equipment racks. They provide vertical and horizontal fixing points to support and position rack mounted equipment.
Used to secure rack mountable equipment such as servers, network switches, patch panels, and shelves within a rack cabinet.
Non electrical, non mechanical components that do not perform an independent mechanical or electrical function.
Supplied in pairs of two, they do not make complete racks or cabinets in their own right and are designed to be installed post-delivery.
